# Use privacy-policy-check

<!-- Generated by build_pack_guides.py from pack.json and the skills' own files. Edit those, not this. -->

Check a startup's privacy policy against what its app actually does — a script scans the code's dependencies, script tags and API calls for the services that receive users' data (analytics, ad pixels, session replay, error monitoring, payments, sign-in, email, support chat, AI model APIs, maps), then finds each one the policy doesn't disclose, each policy claim the code contradicts ("we never share your data" beside a Meta pixel), and the sections the policy lacks — and writes the paragraphs to add.

**Reach for it when** a founder asks "is our privacy policy accurate", "does our privacy policy cover everything we use", "check our privacy policy against the app", "we added analytics / OpenAI — do we need to update the policy", or before launch, an app-store review or a customer's security questionnaire.

## Install it

```bash
npx skilldrop-cli install privacy-policy-check                 # Claude Code, your user folder
npx skilldrop-cli install privacy-policy-check --project       # Claude Code, this repo
npx skilldrop-cli install privacy-policy-check --ide cursor    # or kiro, codex, antigravity, copilot
```

It is part of the Startup legal pack: [`--pack startup-legal`](../packs/use-the-startup-legal-pack.md) installs it with its neighbours.

It ships scripts, so it needs Python 3 (standard library only, nothing to install). What they may touch is declared in [its manifest](../../../packs/startup-legal/skills/privacy-policy-check/manifest.json).

## Ask for it

Say it the way you would to a colleague. Requests like these route to it:

- "Is our privacy policy accurate for what the app actually does?"
- "We added OpenAI and PostHog, do we need to update the privacy policy?"
- "Check our privacy policy against the code before the App Store review"
- "Does our privacy policy cover all the third parties we use?"

Requests like these belong to a different skill, so it shouldn't answer them:

- "Do a DPIA for our new face-matching feature"
- "Answer this customer's security questionnaire"
- "Map our SOC 2 controls to evidence"

If another skill answers instead, ask for this one by name: "use privacy-policy-check".

## Check what you get

A good result:

- **Every service named comes from the scan,** with its file and line or its package.
- **Every contradiction quotes the policy's sentence** and names the code that contradicts it.
- **Every gap has paste-ready text** that names the service, what it receives and why.
- **Dev-only tools aren't reported** as services that receive users' data.
- **What the code can't show is listed as questions,** not guessed.
- **The reply leads with what is untrue,** with no mention of scripts, files inside the skill or the skill itself.

- [habit app](../../../packs/startup-legal/skills/privacy-policy-check/examples/habit-app.md)

## Use something else when

- Writing a privacy policy for a product with no code yet: describe the data flows first
- A full data protection impact assessment for high-risk processing: that is a DPIA
- Terms of service, cookie banners and consent flows: this checks the policy's statements
- Contracts with vendors (data processing agreements): check the agreement itself
